newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says corruption threatens Russian security.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says corruption threatens Russian security.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday described corruption as a threat to the security of Russia and said he was sure his government would win the age-long battle against graft.

"In Russia there will be an authoritative and efficient state power," Yeltsin said in a radio address. "Corruption is one of the main reasons that the authority of the Russian state is low today. This is preventing us from bringing order to the country and threatening the very security of Russia."
Yeltsin said Russia would introduce open tenders for state orders from May 1 in order to reduce the possibility of wrong-doing by state officials.
He admitted that the task would not be easy. "I know that you will nevertheless have your doubts about our victory over corruption," he said.
"But I am determined, I have the political will and I have your backing in this fight. I will bring this difficult struggle to an end. It will become scary to steal and to take bribes."

Yeltsin, who has returned resolutely to the political fray after eight months absence with heart problems and pneumonia, has adopted radio addresses as his favourite mode of addressing the Russian people.
